task: Security lens over lane 2 (uncommitted working tree vs 8c62720): travel state, clock advance, URL history. Is the only new address input the debug travel call; does a travel string reach anything but RNG keys and textContent; can advanceClock write a URL that parseUrlState then rejects; can start()/init(attempt) leave two renderers or leak listeners; any new fetch/storage/secret; is status.html still inert; can a crafted link alone grow resources.
verdict: CONCERNS (low, nothing blocking, no exposure), then two LOW findings fixed in the same commit before it landed. Claims 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 confirmed by reading the full flow plus a grep over all of src/. Claim 3 split: the advanceClock guard (negative/non-finite) holds, but its 'the arrival can always be written' half was REFUTED at both boundaries. Pinned: a crafted ?t=1e20 plus one maximum in-galaxy warp (d <= 1e21 m, dt <= 9.13e9 s) produces t ~= 1.0000000000913e20, which formatNumber writes and parseUrlState rejects on reload, silently dropping the pin. Live: a crafted ?epoch=0001-01-01 plus one maximum jump writes a negative-year ISO string that fails the four-digit pattern, resetting the epoch to 2000 (a multi-millennium jump); at ~600 accumulated jumps toISOString throws inside urlForState, before pushState. Neither is reachable from a link alone, but both break ADR-0012's round-trip claim.
notes: Fix: advanceClock now returns a result union (ok:true with the clock, or ok:false with a plain reason), and refuses an arrival whose clock is outside what the reader accepts, so the writer cannot produce a state the reader rejects; commitTravel surfaces the reason through the HUD instead of writing the link. Bounds are exported (MIN_EPOCH_MS/MAX_EPOCH_MS) and derived from the reader's own four-digit ISO years rather than re-guessed. Two new tests pin the refusals at both edges, and a third round-trips an in-range pinned and live arrival through urlForState -> parseUrlState with zero issues. F3 (informational) was the missing boundary round-trip test, which would have caught this; now present. F4 (informational) was a note citing .scratch/travel-e2e.mjs as evidence when .scratch is gitignored, so a fresh session could not run it; the probe moved to the tracked tools/ tree as tools/travel-probe.mjs with npm run probe:travel, matching the existing probe convention, and every citation was updated. start()/init cannot leave two live renderers: the generation check at main.ts:277 throws before context.configure and the one at 338-341 disposes the loser; a second start() while an init is in flight sees previous=null but that init attaches listeners only after its final checkpoint. Resource growth from a crafted link alone is impossible: one boot, popstate needs same-document entries that only a committed travel creates, the GPUDevice is a singleton promise, pipelines are GC-reclaimed, and mountHud reuses fixed DOM ids; the only unbounded counter is history.length, one entry per deliberate arrival to a different address, which is the designed behaviour. No secret, credential, absolute path or personal data in any added line; no new network, storage or DOM sink; status.html stays static under its CSP. Cost: cents, one seat, one pass.
